issues.legal_issue: A fresh suit for possession of property allotted under a partition compromise is not barred by the execution requirement when the claimant remained in constructive possession and the occupants held permissively.
material_facts: A partition suit was compromised and the plaint property was allotted to the claimant, but no formal decree was drawn because the parties did not provide the required stamp paper.
The occupants remained physically on the property with permission until they removed a structure they had built there.

The occupants claimed only that they held as tenants; their claim that the claimant had put them in possession under a lease was rejected, and they did not assert a right to possess the property as their own.
The claimant was therefore in constructive possession after the compromise.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s suit for recovery of khas possession was not barred by section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not bar a fresh suit for possession in these circumstances where the claimant remained in constructive possession and the opposing parties’ physical occupation was permissive, rather than possession asserted against the claimant’s title. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: partition_compromise_possession_suit and no_formal_decree_drawn and claimant_constructively_possessed and occupants_remained_permissively and occupants_acknowledged_claimant_title

predicates.partition_compromise_possession_suit: A claimant brings a suit for possession of property allotted to the claimant under a partition compromise.
predicates.no_formal_decree_drawn: No formal decree was drawn up after the compromise.
predicates.claimant_constructively_possessed: The claimant retained constructive possession of the property after the compromise.
predicates.occupants_remained_permissively: The opposing occupants remained physically on the property with permission rather than intending to possess it as their own.
predicates.occupants_acknowledged_claimant_title: The opposing occupants claimed no right to remain in possession other than a derivative right, and their asserted basis for that right was not established.

issues.definition: When a claimant sues for property allotted under a partition compromise, no decree was drawn, the claimant remained in constructive possession, and the occupants stayed permissively while acknowledging the claimant’s title, the fresh possession suit is not barred by the execution requirement.

issues.legal_issue: Constructive possession of a homestead is sufficient to support retention of the property as a tenant when it vests in the State, even if the claimant is not in physical possession.
material_facts: The plaint property was a homestead covered by section 5 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1959, and vested in the State while the possession suit was pending.
Although the claimant was not physically occupying the property, the occupants remained there permissively after the partition compromise, so the claimant was in constructive possession at vesting.
Section 5 speaks of possession, whereas section 6 expressly speaks of khas possession.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was in possession for the purpose of section 5, became entitled to retain the homestead as a tenant under the State free of rent, and could maintain the suit for possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1959, possession of a homestead at vesting is sufficient for retention as a tenant under the State free of rent; unlike section 6, section 5 does not require khas possession. Constructive possession is sufficient. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: homestead_vesting_possession_case and property_is_homestead and claimant_constructively_possessed_at_vesting and retention_requires_only_possession

predicates.homestead_vesting_possession_case: A claim to retain a homestead arises after the property vests in the State while a possession suit is pending.
predicates.property_is_homestead: The property falls within the category of homestead covered by the applicable retention rule.
predicates.claimant_constructively_possessed_at_ves: At the time of vesting, the claimant had constructive possession despite another person’s permissive physical occupation.
predicates.retention_requires_only_possession: The applicable retention rule requires possession but does not require exclusive physical possession or khas possession.

issues.definition: When a homestead vests in the State, the claimant was constructively in possession at vesting, and the retention rule requires possession rather than khas possession, a suit to recover the homestead is maintainable.
